To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR Prep — capacity scenarios, GPU spend sensitivity & operational ask matrix

Team —

We need a tight package for the QBR deck on infra capacity and unit economics. The board wants: a crisp run-rate ask (3 slides), a sensitivity view for GPU spend vs. utilization, and a short operational ask matrix (decisions we need from leadership with owners and deadlines). Please treat this as the canonical thread for inputs.

Immediate asks (deliverables / owners / due):
- Capacity model v3 (single-sheet, assumptions tab): karthik — populate with weekly utilization per pool + committed vs spot mix (due Tue 11/2 EOD). See attached starter model.
- Batching & cache experiment summary: irene — top-line latency/cost delta for our RPS mix and any regressions noticed (due Wed 11/3 AM). Please include raw logs stub and the experiment config.
- Vendor pricing and commitment options: vivek — latest quotes from AvaCloud and estimated break-even points for reserved vs on-demand for 6/12/24 month terms (due Wed 11/3 EOD).
- One-pager for Leadership: lauren + marissa — I will draft; I need your comments on the ask matrix by Thu 11/4.

Notes & scope: focus on query-generation workloads (avg seq len 128, p95 token rate), include KV-cache hit scenarios (0%, 25%, 50%), and batching at 8/16/32. We will show both short-term (quarter) and runway (9 month) implications.

Attachments: QBR_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (starter sheet).

Thanks — please reply inline for anything that changes scope.

--
Lauren Bishop
Director, Infrastructure Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QBR Prep — capacity scenarios, GPU spend sensitivity & operational ask matrix

Lauren / team —

Quick update on the capacity model inputs (attached: snapshot exported to CSV) and a couple clarifying asks:

Top-line numbers (current week baseline):
- Aggregated GPU utilization (prod pools): 68% avg (p95 CPU/kernel skew drives tail).
- Effective token-rate: 11.2M tokens/day (hosted + dedicated).
- Current monthly GPU spend (cloud): ~$1.32M (includes ephemeral spots and reserved amortized).

Scenario notes I put into v3:
- If KV-cache hit = 25% and batching = 16, we project a ~22% reduction in tokens-served GPU-time, which maps to ~18% unit-cost reduction assuming identical throughput SLA.
- With batching = 32 we see further marginal gains but tail latency increases—p95 latency goes from 380ms -> 560ms in our sim for seq=128. Need decision tolerance for p95 SLA.

Questions:
1) For the sensitivity slides: do we want to show vendor break-even at token cost or at monthly commit level? I can produce both but they change the framing.
2) Is the runway view expected to include potential model-downsizing (quantization) scenarios or keep model architecture fixed?

I attached a CSV export (quick snapshot) and updated the assumptions tab in QBR_capacity_model_v3.xlsx.

-Karthik
Engineering Manager, Capacity & Orchestration
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-02T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QBR Prep — capacity scenarios, GPU spend sensitivity & operational ask matrix

Adding the batching/cache experiment top-line here. Attaching the logs bundle (batching-cache-experiment-logs.zip) with experiment IDs and run configs.

Experiment highlights (RPS mix that matches product baseline):
- Baseline (no batching, no KV cache): median 120ms, p95 320ms, cost baseline = 1.00x.
- KV-cache @25% (no batching): median 110ms, p95 300ms, cost = 0.85x.
- Batching @16 + KV-cache 25%: median 140ms, p95 420ms, cost = 0.70x.
- Batching @32 + KV-cache 50%: median 210ms, p95 680ms, cost = 0.56x (note increased tail).

Operational notes:
- The cache hit rates above assume perfect prefix reuse; for some enterprise workloads (long-form generation) hit-rate is lower. We tagged runs by workload and included percent of requests affected.
- We saw two regressions in structured-output tests when batching=32 (truncation edge-cases). Those are logged under EXP-2026-11-01-#7.

Ask for leadership: acceptable p95 SLA threshold for interactive endpoints (recommendation: keep p95 <= 500ms for hosted tier; allow higher for dedicated bulk workloads).

Irene
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: QBR Prep — capacity scenarios, GPU spend sensitivity & operational ask matrix (final asks + leadership decisions)

Thanks for the fast turn. Consolidated decisions and asks below — this goes to exec slides tomorrow morning.

Decisions / framing (for slides):
- Show both break-even views: per-token unit-cost and monthly commit. Vivek will annotate vendor quotes on slide 5. (Action: vivek — attach vendor quote snippets to the drive doc by 11/03 EOD).
- Runway scenarios will keep model architecture fixed but include a single quantized+int8 sensitivity line (to show upside) — Karthik to add a 4th column in the model v3. (Action: karthik — update model v3 by 11/02 EOD was fine; please add quantized row by 11/04 AM).
- Operational ask matrix (slide 7): accept batching up to 16 for hosted interactive with KV-cache 25% as primary lever; reserve batching=32 as a gated experiment for dedicated/bulk. Irene to include risk lines and regression flags.

Final action list (owner / deliverable / due):
- Karthik: add quantized sensitivity row + finalize assumptions tab (due 11/04 09:00).
- Irene: attach experiment logs + short risk appendix with EXP-2026-11-01-#7 flagged (done; logs attached).
- Vivek: vendor quote snippets + break-even calc (due 11/03 EOD).
- Marissa & Lauren: finalize leadership one-pager + recommended ask (draft in drive; comments by 11/04 noon).

I will roll this into the QBR deck and circulate to execs by Tue morning. If anyone has dissent on the batching=16 recommendation for hosted interactive, raise now — otherwise we'll present this as our recommended operational lever.

Attachments referenced: QBR_capacity_model_v3.xlsx, batching-cache-experiment-logs.zip, qbr_one_pager.pdf

--
Lauren Bishop
Director, Infrastructure Strategy
